#2231. Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

Rangers manager Derek McInnes has stated Falkirk's win over Celtic was "not really a shock".

The Ibrox boss commented on the weekend result when he appeared on talkSPORT on Monday morning, as he hailed the work done by John McGlynn.

Ally McCoist had singled out McGlynn for praise for the job he has done at Falkirk - and McInnes joined in on heaping praise on the manager.

And he insisted it wasn't a huge shock to see Falkirk beat Celtic.

On talkSPORT, McInnes said: "The likes of John, you like to see good managers doing good jobs.

Clearly they lost a few good players, and that's normally the way. It's difficult to keep them - especially at a club like Falkirk.

"You just see a good manager doing his work well.

"Although it seems a shock Celtic getting beat there, but it's not really a shock when you see it's Falkirk that win the game.

"Falkirk are capable of that, and they did that a couple of times last season as well."

McInnes then backed his former club Hearts to be in the title hunt this season.

He said: "I do think Hearts will be title contenders again with the investment and size of squad they have got and the level of player they have got.

"I think Hearts will be up there again. It will be more of a surprise if they're not."

#2230. "Anna Frank laziale": ancora scritte antisemite a Donna Olimpia | FOTO

Il minisindaco e l’assessora Alessia Salmoni si sono recati sul posto per organizzare il ripristino del decoro.

Nuove scritte antisemite sono comparse sui muri di un condominio a Donna Olimpia, nel municipio XII. Secondo quanto riportato da Roma Today, Tra queste c’è «Anna Frank laziale». Il minisindaco Elio Tomassetti ha denunciato l’episodio, rilevato nella mattinata di lunedì 2 novembre, a nove giorni da un caso simile nella stessa zona.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Tomassetti ha segnalato la ricomparsa di scritte antisemite e slogan neofascisti nel quartiere. «Questi continui atti non cambieranno la storia del nostro quartiere», ha dichiarato. Ha poi definito quello degli autori «un atteggiamento vigliacco», riferendosi a chi scrive di notte e si nasconde di giorno.

Secondo il minisindaco, chi lascia quegli slogan macchia gli spazi del quartiere con messaggi che non troveranno posto nel municipio XII. A riferire la denuncia è Roma Today.

Tomassetti ha annunciato di essersi recato sul posto insieme all’assessora Alessia Salmoni. I due hanno espresso solidarietà ai condomini e si sono occupati di organizzare le attività per il ripristino del decoro.

Il minisindaco ha detto di avere fiducia nel lavoro delle forze dell’ordine, che ha descritto come da sempre al fianco del municipio nel condannare e perseguire atti simili. Ha inoltre ribadito che le forze democratiche e antifasciste del municipio XII continueranno a opporsi a queste azioni. Richiamando la storia antifascista del quartiere, ha affermato che la comunità «non indietreggerà di un solo passo».

#2228. ‘All of a sudden’: Sheffield United in strong position ahead of next three fixtures, says EFL expert

Sheffield United have risen up to 10th in the league after their first 13 fixtures and they are three points off the play-offs behind West Ham in 8th. SUFC won 1-0 at home against Wrexham last time out with Ben Brereton Diaz getting their goal.

The Blades are back in action on Tuesday evening with an away trip to Deepdale to face rock bottom Preston North End. They then face struggling Charlton Athletic and Watford.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the South Yorkshire outfit on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Maybe the most impressed I’ve been with them this season (against Wrexham). That is quite a lot bar to clear I will say. (Romelle) Donovan looked good. I think increasingly (Michael) Cooper in goal, (Japhet) Tanganga and (Liam) Kitching at centre-back, (Sydie) Peck and (Kalvin) Phillips in midfield, it’s quite a nice spine.

“All of a sudden they’re up in 10th Sheffield United having had what felt like a really poor start to the season. They’ve got Preston next away and then Charlton away, after the break Watford at home so 10th right now with three fixtures on paper against teams right down at the bottom.”

On his day, Sheffield United goalkeeper Michael Cooper is one of the best players in his position in the division. He is then backed up on the bench by the experienced Adam Davies.

The Blades have been solid defensively so far in this campaign. Cooper has kept five clean sheets along with Stoke City’s Viktor Johansson and Birmingham City’s James Beadle, with only Swansea City’s Lawrence Vigouroux keeping more.

As Maxwell has alluded to, Japhet Tanganga and Liam Kitching have formed a solid partnership in the heart of defence. The latter joined from Premier League new boys Coventry City in the summer and he has made a positive impression.

Sheffield United have useful full-backs like Femi Seriki and Harrison Burrows who like to get up and down the flank. Further up the pitch, Kalvin Phillips, Sydie Peck and Oli Arblaster are all good options to have in the middle of the park.

Patrick Bamford is a proven goal scorer up top for Wilder’s side. They also have dangerous attackers including Brereton Diaz, Romelle Donovan, Tom Cannon and Tyrese Campbell at their disposal as well so the competition and depth is decent.

Despite not being able to spend much money in the last transfer window, Sheffield United still have a strong squad. SUFC also have an experienced manager in Wilder.

There is no reason why the Blades can’t push for the play-offs this term. They have a nice blend of youth and experience in their ranks.

They will need to be at their best to get a win against Preston North End, regardless of the Lilywhites’ position and poor form. No game is easy and Wilder will be aware that it could be a potential banana skin for his players.

#2227. Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

Rangers icon Ally McCoist has revealed he would hate to see Celtic boss Martin O'Neill suffer and reckons the veteran manager has earned the right to walk away on his own terms.

The Ibrox hero, who has long admired O'Neill despite their rivalry, admits his biggest concern is the toll management can take on the 74-year-old's health. While McCoist hopes close friend Derek McInnes can guide Rangers to title glory this season, he stressed he would take no pleasure in seeing O'Neill pushed out of Parkhead or forced to continue beyond the point where the job remains enjoyable.

The former Rangers striker believes O'Neill's decades of service to the game, and his achievements at Celtic, mean he deserves the respect to decide for himself when the time is right to step aside.

Speaking to talkSPORT Bet Online Casino, the 64-year-old said: "I think Martin has absolutely earned the right and deserves the respect to stay for as long as he feels right. I really do.

"I would hate Martin to overstay his time at Celtic, first and foremost for his health.

Read more: Rangers boss Derek McInnes brands Falkirk win over Celtic 'not really a shock'

"That's the most important thing, because I've always gotten on really well with Martin. Obviously I want Rangers to win the league 100 per cent, but Martin has more than earned the right to see things out for as long as he wants at Celtic, and that should be the case."

McCoist also concedes Europe's demands could yet play a significant role in the title race.

"I don't think for a minute Martin will say they're prioritising, but their level of performance in Europe has been extremely disappointing. I know they created one or two chances against Benfica, but Benfica were three-nil up and done.

"The performances in Europe have been really disappointing from Martin's point of view.

"I don't have any doubt that it could work in Rangers' favour not having those Thursday European games. Celtic are not allowed, same as Rangers, to get into any game other than expecting to win, particularly at home, whether domestic or European, the fans won't allow it.

"So there is added pressure on Celtic, of course there is. But Martin will be delighted with their league form. I noticed a lovely quote from him this morning where he said it was a fantastic result at the weekend, but if they get beaten on Thursday there'll be another crisis!

#2225. Brocchi: "La Lazio di Gattuso somiglia alla mia. Dove può arrivare? Vi dico che..."

Il primato in classifica e il momento straordinario che sta attraversando la Lazio di Gattuso non sono passati inosservati agli ex biancocelesti. In particolare, a parlarne è stato Cristian Brocchi sulle colonne de La Repubblica. L'ex centrocampista biancoceleste, protagonista della Lazio del 2010 di Reja, visse un inizio campionato molto simile a quello dell'attuale formazione laziale. Di seguito l'intervista.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L’entusiasmo con cui questa squadra scende in campo, è lo stesso che avevamo noi. E anche allora eravamo reduci da una stagione difficile e sofferta, siamo stati capaci di trasformare negatività e scetticismo in energia positiva, proprio come questa Lazio. Nessuno voleva rivivere le sensazioni dell’anno prima. E poi il mercato. Nel gennaio precedente, parliamo del 2010, arrivarono giocatori importanti come Biava, Dias e Floccari, che si integrarono subito e sistemarono la squadra. Così siamo partiti, pochi mesi dopo, con uno spirito diverso e più certezze. Stessa cosa è successa con Taylor: arrivato a gennaio 2026, è uno dei perni della formazione di Gattuso, un grande calciatore.

Si rivede in qualche centrocampista della Lazio di oggi? Stimo molto Frattesi, che ho allenato al Monza. Dico sempre che dentro ha il 50% di Brocchi, cioè la mentalità vincente e la voglia di lottare, l’altro 50% è l’abilità in zona gol, che io non avevo. In tv, a inizio campionato, avevo detto che avrebbe potuto competere per l’Europa, perché ha giocatori di valore con caratteristiche adatte al calcio di Gattuso. Lui ha sempre creduto in questo gioco aggressivo, non è cambiato. Però ora non alziamo troppo l’asticella, a Roma è pericoloso, lo so bene, poi bastano un paio di passi falsi e subito si dice che è finita la magia o la benzina. Si passa dall’euforia allo sconforto in un attimo. È successo anche a noi, quando perdemmo il primo posto dopo le sconfitte nel derby e a Cesena. E a gennaio ricordo le polemiche perché ci si aspettava più rinforzi sul mercato (arrivò solo Sculli, ndr). Bisogna procedere partita dopo partita, con realismo, e reagire bene ai momenti negativi.

Obiettivi? Per come si sta esprimendo adesso, anche questa squadra può lottare per entrare tra le prime quattro: avevo previsto che si sarebbe classificata tra la sesta e l’ottava posizione, ora dico tra la quarta e la sesta. Il percorso però è lungo, le big sono più abituate a fare punti pesanti, impossibile sottovalutarle. E ci saranno tanti scontri diretti da affrontare. Ma se la Lazio sarà così in alto anche alla vigilia degli ultimi due mesi, allora tutto potrà succedere.

Gattuso? Ha rivitalizzato calciatori forti che non avevano reso secondo il loro valore. Penso in particolare a Tavares e Zaccagni: con Sarri, che considero comunque un grande allenatore, erano come leoni in gabbia, Rino li ha liberati e ora fanno la differenza. Anche Noslin, Isaksen e lo stesso Taylor rendono molto di più. Provstgaard non giocava, adesso è un titolare.

Ha un sogno, Gattuso? Conoscendolo, vorrebbe rivedere l’Olimpico pieno. Io sono molto legato al popolo biancoceleste, è fantastico: quando firmai per la Lazio ero felice perché da avversario ero incantato dall’atmosfera di quello stadio e finalmente sarebbe stato il mio campo. Quindi capisco il sogno di Rino, spero riesca a realizzarlo.

#2224. David Storch ‘delighted’ but urges ‘patience’ as Sheffield Wednesday appoint Dave Challinor

Sheffield Wednesday have named Dave Challinor as the permanent successor to Henrik Pedersen after the Dane’s departure in October. The 51-year-old takes charge of SWFC on a contract until 2030 with Clint Hill and Anthony Sweeney joining as assistant coaches.

The move has sparked excitement among the Hillsborough faithful, and chairman David Storch is “delighted” with the appointment too. However, the Owls chief issued a strong reminder of the need for patience as Wednesday rebuild.

In his first words on Challinor’s arrival, Storch said: “We are still at the beginning of an ambitious journey. Significant progress has been made in rebuilding the foundations of the club, but we recognise there is much more work ahead.

“Our ambitions remain clear, but our progress cannot be defined by the outcome of one moment or season alone. We must establish a clear footballing identity, consistent standards and a culture capable of delivering sustained success. That journey will require patience, resilience and collective commitment. Progress will not always be straightforward, but we believe Dave has the leadership, character and determination to help us achieve our ambitions.”

There is excitement over Challinor’s arrival at Hillsborough, and it is justified. The new Sheffield Wednesday boss led Stockport County from the National League to the top end of League One, and he was a hit in previous jobs at Hartlepool United and AFC Fylde beforehand.

After moving on Pedersen and bringing in Challinor, fans will set high expectations. The Owls sit 9th, so the hope will be that the new boss can deliver progress and lift them further into the promotion conversation.

However, Storch’s words emphasise the need for patience, and perhaps indicate that Challinor will not be judged on whether or not this season is a success. Success would be defined as a top-six finish at the very least by many, given the strength of SWFC’s squad, but it appears that the club hierarchy are not going to demand that in the immediate future.

Instead, Storch’s comments indicate that Wednesday want to build towards those heights with three goals: a footballing identity, consistent standards and a strong culture. It suggests a quick ascent is not what is being demanded or expected, which does conflict with the hopes of sections of the support after Pedersen’s sacking.

Challinor’s track record and availability meant he was viewed by many as a shoo-in for the Sheffield Wednesday job. His trajectory matches the one desired by SWFC, and he has the promotion credentials to his name to lead the club out of League One.

The Chester-born boss has done an excellent job of building cultures at his former clubs and this is a clear desire of Storch and the other decision-makers at Hillsborough. The chairman’s words indicate he will be given the time to do so with the Owls.

Storch’s vision is a long-term one, and Challinor will help him fulfil the goals set out as Wednesday rebuild after relegation and administration. The fans want results though, so time will tell if the new boss can satisfy everyone in a demanding job at a big club.

Redknapp, who both played for and managed the Hammers, has delivered his verdict on talkSPORT: “Scott’s got a great record in the Championship and has taken teams up. He knows the club. He was a very, very good player. I took him from West Ham to Tottenham. Good lad. He’s a very astute manager. I think he’s a great fit for West Ham.”

He added: “He hasn’t got an easy job on his hands. Take (Jarrod) Bowen apart, there’s very few players there who would have got into too many West Ham teams over the years. They’ve got great support, it’s a big club that unfortunately needs a big lift now.”

Parker played 129 games for West Ham during his playing days. As well as WHUFC, he also had spells at Charlton Athletic, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Tottenham Hotspur and Fulham.

The ex-England international, who made 18 caps for his country, hung up his boots in 2017. He has since delved into the managerial world.

He started coaching at Spurs before returning to Fulham as their manager in 2019. He guided the Whites to promotion to the Premier League in 2020 before doing the same with AFC Bournemouth two years later.

The London-born man also got Burnley up in 2025 so he knows what it takes to get out of the EFL. He has also managed abroad following a stint at Club Brugge in Belgium before his switch to Turf Moor.

As Redknapp has alluded to, Parker has promotion experience and knows West Ham well already. He should be able to get the WHUFC fans onside.

The Hammers need to find some form as they look to claw themselves back into the top flight at the first time of asking. They are in the top eight along with Wolves, West Brom, Southampton, Birmingham City and Stoke City as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Swansea City.

They lost 3-1 at home against West Brom last time out and were poor against the Baggies. They are back in action on Wednesday night with an away trip to South Wales to take on Cardiff City as they aim to get themselves back on track and return to winning ways.

West Ham managed to keep hold of Jarrod Bowen in the last transfer window. He has been prolific so far this term but needs some of his teammates to step up now.

The London outfit will get the chance to bolster their ranks this winter. They will also have the opportunity to let some players head out the exit door as well in January.

#2219. Rangers star called up by under-21 national team after being dropped from full squad

Rangers star Kim Min-su has been named in South Korea's under-21 squad instead, after he was dropped from their full squad.

The Ibrox ace made his international debut for his country last month and played in three friendlies against Ecuador, Uruguay and Venezuela and was an unused sub against Uzbekistan.

But that wasn't enough to see him included in South Korea's latest squad for their games against Qatar and Saudi Arabia later this month.

However, he has now been included in their under-21s squad for two friendlies against Mexico.

The squad doubles as South Korea's Olympic team for the football section of the Games in two years' time in Los Angeles.

South Korea Under 21s boss Kim Eun-joong said: "This is a good opportunity to gain practical experience against a strong team, Mexico.

"We will identify areas for improvement and take our competitiveness up a level."

Kim will travel to his homeland for the two games against the Mexicans at Cheonan on November 14 and a rematch against the same opponents three days later at the same venue.

#2216. 'I thought I was watching The Karate Kid' - top ref rages at Rangers VAR escape

Mark Clattenburg has called out Ryan Lee and John Beaton after insisting Rangers' James Penrice should have been sent off during the Scottish League Cup semi-final win over Aberdeen.

The former FIFA referee was left stunned after Penrice escaped punishment for a first-half challenge on Aremu Afeez before going on to set up Ryan Naderi's late winner as Rangers booked their place in the final at Hampden.

Penrice, operating in midfield alongside Nicolas Raskin, escaped punishment after missing the ball and catching Aberdeen's Afeez with a high, studs-up challenge near the halfway line.

Referee Lee opted against showing a card, while VAR official Beaton chose not to intervene.

Read more: Martin O'Neill sent health plea from worried Rangers hero as Celtic rivalry parked

The decision has come under intense scrutiny, with Clattenburg unable to believe Penrice remained on the pitch.

Speaking on the So Near, Yet So VAR podcast, he said: “I thought I wasn’t even watching football. I was watching my favourite, The Karate Kid.

“Listen, it’s more justifiable and easier to understand when the ball isn’t really that high. If you look at it again, the ball isn’t really there, and I think the player knows what he’s doing.”

Clattenburg went on to explain why he believes the challenge was impossible to defend.

He said: “I think he’s just decided he wants to catch his opponent high with his studs.

“And when you’re playing the ball, when you’re trying to play, you don’t go in like that. You would go in with your body. You would go in with your knee.

“You don’t go in with your studs and then make a clear movement with the studs towards an opponent’s ribs, hip, wherever we want to call it.

“I was surprised it wasn’t red. I’ve seen it in real time.

“For me, when it’s not a footballing action, then you can never support a player’s actions, and I think when a referee gives a red, then nobody can have any argument.”

Former SPFL referee Bobby Madden agreed with Clattenburg's assessment, with both officials adamant Rangers should have been reduced to 10 men.

The controversy was heightened when Penrice went on to have a decisive impact on the result, providing the assist for Naderi's 83rd-minute winner that secured Rangers' place in the final.

Aberdeen will feel particularly aggrieved given the match-winning contribution came from a player many believe should already have been dismissed.

Clattenburg and Madden are not alone in that opinion. Former SFA referee Des Roache has also argued that Penrice should have been sent off for the challenge on Afeez.

#2215. Veteran with 522 EFL caps backs Lincoln City 23-year-old for ‘a big future’

Lincoln City have fared fairly well in their first 13 games of the 2026/27 Championship season, sitting in 16th with 15 points to their name. The Imps spent on new players like Mikkel Ladefoged and Andrei Coubis in the summer, but among those to impress on the step up from League One has been Deji Elerewe.

Now, the 23-year-old centre-back has received high praise from defensive partner and EFL veteran Sonny Bradley. Speaking to the club’s official media, he said: “I recognised it before the first couple of weeks that he came in the door. I could tell straight away in training that he was a big lad. He was aggressive, he was ready to get stuck in and everything that he was asked to do, he could do comfortably.

“I recognised pretty early that he’s got a big future in the game. He’s had a great start to the season, but it’s just the start. With the mentality that he’s got, I’m pretty sure he’ll want to take it into the rest of this year and certainly into the second half of the season.”

Having made 522 EFL appearances across all three leagues, Sonny Bradley knows what he’s talking about when it comes to impressive young prospects. Lincoln City’s stand-in skipper has played alongside and come up against plenty of top talents across his storied career, so his praise of Elerewe comes as a glowing review.

After starting out at Charlton Athletic, Elerewe made a name for himself at Bromley and earned his move to Sincil Bank in the winter. He started encouragingly, but has really stepped up in the Championship.

Elerewe has played all but six minutes of the Championship campaign so far, locking down a starting spot. He’s among the league’s top 13% of centre-backs for defensive contributions (113) and ranks highly for his interceptions (21 – top 7%), aerial duels won (40 – top 11%) and touches in the opposition box (30 – top 4%).

The Imps ace has the physical stature and power to hold his own against big strikers and he serves as an aerial asset in both boxes. At 23, he is of the age and profile to kick on further and challenge himself at a higher level in the years to come.

Elerewe’s progress at his young age means that excitement over his future is more than justified. He has the physical profile to be a success at all levels, so it will be a case of rounding out his game both defensively and in possession to push to new heights.

Lincoln City will have the firm belief that Elerewe can become a high value asset in the transfer market in the years to come. He has quickly grown into an influential player at Sincil Bank, and that will bring admiring glances from clubs higher up in the food chain.

For now though, Elerewe will be focused on the task at hand with the Imps, where he is under contract until 2029. Alongside his own personal development, the goal for this season is to stay in the Championship, and the London-born defender can have a key part to play in that.

#2213. Celtic Europa League rivals make shock decision to sack history-making boss

Celtic's Europa League opponents Torreense have sacked the manager who made history with the Portuguese minnows after they slumped to the bottom half of the country's second tier.

The Hoops face one of the smallest teams ever to play in the league phase of European competition later this month when they play Torreense.

The game will be played in Leiria, 50 miles away from their home of Torres Vedras, because their 2,000-capacity stadium is not suitable.

They made history last season when they defeated Sporting Lisbon in the Portuguese Cup Final under boss Luis Tralhao.

But they have sacked him and replaced him with former Estrela da Amadora manager Joao Nuno instead.

Torreense are languishing in 12th place in the Portuguese second division after a disastrous season so far domestically.

However, they made history when they won in Norway against Lillestrom in their opening game and were only defeated by Sunderland after an injury time goal.

They play Armenian outfit Ararat-Armenia this week - the only team behind Celtic in the table, on goal difference - before welcoming the Parkhead side at the end of the month.

#2211. Cardiff City’s injury struggles continue as Brian Barry-Murphy confirms new blow for attacker

Cardiff City face West Ham on Wednesday night, the league’s highest scorers. It marks another tough game in a challenging run of fixtures, and the Bluebirds will be without forward Isaak Davies after a new injury blow.

Brian Barry-Murphy confirmed to BBC Sport Wales that Davies will face four weeks on the sidelines with a hamstring issue. Unfortunately for the City boss, the Welsh attacker is not the only concern, with Perry Ng and Alex Robertson in need of assessment while Dylan Lawlor, Calum Chambers, and Callum Robinson have been out too.

Robinson has been omitted from the last three matchday squads, but the decision has not been expanded on since Barry-Murphy first said ‘certain standards’ had not been met.

Aside from a loan spell in Belgium, Isaak Davies has always played for Cardiff City. He joined the club when he was seven, making his professional debut against Middlesbrough in October 2021 and scoring his first goal against Preston North End in January 2022.

Fans have a natural affection for the player because of his affiliation with the club. However, he has struggled to make a mark on the first team for the most part, and that has continued this term.

Davies has only played 74 minutes of Championship football so far this season, and he is yet to score. His highest goalscoring season for the Bluebirds is six goals, compared to 12 scored in a productive loan spell with KV Kortrijk.

He’s had injury absences to deal with too, impacting his bid to find consistency. It will be hoped this latest blow does not result in an extended spell on the sidelines with four weeks the initial timescale.

Although the news about Davies is a blow, defensive injuries are more of a concern at Cardiff City currently. The Bluebirds will operate with Yousef Salech up front and have the option of Jack Moylan should he be required.

However, defensively, they are without Lawlor, Chambers and Bielik, amongst others. It meant Barry-Murphy had to utilise Joel Colwill and Ollie Tanner as emergency full-backs at the end of the 3-0 defeat to Wolves.

Despite their defensive injuries, City haven’t done too badly at the back in terms of their performances. They have conceded 20 goals, less than nine other teams in the division.

The Bluebirds will be looking to take advantage of their upcoming fixtures, with games against the likes of Norwich City and Preston North End on the horizon. They will be hoping their injury problems ease as soon as possible to give themselves the best possible chance of taking the points in those matches.

#2208. Under-fire figure eyed Leicester City boss Russell Martin for top Premier League job in 2024

Leicester City hired Russell Martin in the summer, bringing him in to lead their rebuild after relegation from the Championship. The LCFC boss has faced criticism for inconsistent performances and a frustrating style of play, but it wasn’t long ago that he was held in very high regard.

Martin’s work at MK Dons, Swansea City and in winning promotion to the Premier League with Southampton saw him build a strong reputation in the game. So much so, Manchester United sporting director Jason Wilcox – who worked with Martin at St. Mary’s – put him forward as a candidate to monitor when the Red Devils were considering their Erik ten Hag replacements in 2024.

Wilcox viewed Martin as someone to monitor and consider for the role in the future, rather than as an immediate option. This was shortly before the 2024 FA Cup final in May, so around the same time as the Championship play-off final, which the Saints won.

Wilcox moved from Manchester City to Southampton in 2023, stepping into a director of football role for the first time. He would hire Martin from Swansea City shortly after, and the two found success together.

With Martin as manager and Wilcox as a director, the Saints would win immediate promotion back to the Premier League. It saw the stocks of both surge, but the boss stayed put while Wilcox was tempted away to become technical director in a new-look Manchester United hierarchy, before seeing his title switched to director of football.

Neither have found the same fortunes since though. Martin was eventually sacked by Southampton as they sat bottom of the Premier League table, and a dismal 17-game spell at Rangers led to his next managerial opportunity coming in League One with Leicester City.

Wilcox meanwhile remains at Manchester United, but he has been under-fire for shortcomings in recruitment. Many supporters pin their continued struggles on him, and he was in the line of fire when defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club hierarchy too.

Managerial stock comes and goes, and few have experienced the highs and lows quite like Martin. His work in rebuilding Southampton and getting them promoted earned rave reviews, and rightly so.

However, he stuck by his playing principles on the step up to the Premier League, and it backfired badly. Some would argue he has never really recovered from that, with criticisms over his playing style following him to Rangers and Leicester City, and his willingness to speak up and stick to his guns while speaking to the press brings ridicule.

Despite this, he is still a young manager at only 40, and his CV shows how he can rebuild struggling clubs and build a philosophy for fans, players and staff alike to buy into.

Martin is trying to replicate his past success at Leicester City. He faces an uphill battle to do so, but that will not deter him as both he and LCFC fight to return to their previous heights.

#2206. Jamie McGrath hopeful Hibernian heroics in cup clash can lift league fortunes

Jamie McGrath hopes Hibernian’s cup heroics can help revive their wobbling William Hill Premiership campaign.

Hibs went into the Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash against Hearts at Hampden on Sunday bottom of the league, having lost four out of four against their city rivals at the national stadium and with Marink Reedijk looking for his first win as boss at the fifth attempt.

It looked like another day of disappointment was on the cards for the Leith side when Jambos attacker Claudio Braga headed in from a Calvin Miller corner with only four minutes on the clock.

However, Hibs fought back and striker Martin Boyle deservedly levelled in the 19th minute and McGrath struck three minutes before the interval with his first goal of the season to ultimately set up a meeting with Rangers in the final at the national stadium on December 13.

Hibs are one point behind second-bottom Kilmarnock ahead of the trip to Aberdeen on Saturday and McGrath, 30, said: “It was a good feeling obviously to give back to the travelling fans.

“We haven’t given them too much to shout about so far this season, so I think they would have bitten your hand off for a win in Hampden against Hearts.

“But yeah, it’s obviously a great feeling, into a cup final now, so something to look forward to.

“Hopefully now this is the start of us getting a turn on things and building on that.

“We have to get our league form back on track because that hasn’t been good enough.

“I think over the last few weeks we’ve shown what we can do in spells.

“It’s just about getting a full 90-minute performance because even on Sunday we were probably on top for a large period of game.

“I know you can’t control the full 90 minutes, but we’re still adapting to what the manager wants and I think when you see on Sunday when it clicks, it can be really, really good, but it’s about keep working hard now.

“We have to build on these small details, Every day is something new for us to be learning and we’re heavily on the video clips and we’re all buying into it. So, yeah, we’re slowly but surely getting there.”

McGrath’s crucial counter after midfielder Joe Newell’s powerful low drive had been blocked off the line and the Republic of Ireland international quickly tucked the ball in at the near post.

He said: “The ball just fell and the next thing I know it was in the back of the net so I didn’t even know how to celebrate or whatever.

“It’s obviously my first of the season, so it’s been a bit of a frustrating period for myself with a few injuries and niggles and stuff like that.

“But hopefully now we can all kind of stay as fit as we can, the squad’s kind of coming back to full fitness over the next few weeks, so hopefully it’s all clicking at the right time.”

#2205. Allegri a SKY: “Siamo pochi, ci serve una gara di sofferenza. Prendiamo gol facili da evitare”

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, ha parlato a Sky Sport alla vigilia del match di Champions League contro il Porto: “Infortuni? In allenamento non riusciamo a fare il torello coprendo il cerchio di centrocampo. Dobbiamo preparare la partita, è difficile perché il Porto è un’ottima squadra in casa. Noi dobbiamo fare una gara di sofferenza che credo ci serva anche. Mancano piccoli dettagli per portare a casa i risultati, la dimostrazione è l’alternanza di risultati che stiamo facendo in campionato. In Champions, indipendentemente da questa gara, il destino è nelle nostre mani. Con dieci punti si può andare ai playoff, dovrebbe essere un bel traguardo. In quei momenti ci vuole carattere, voglia di portare a casa il risultato in cui abbiamo lasciato tanti punti e preso tanti gol è una situazione di partita che va migliorata. Bisogno di sofferenza? Ogni tanto soffrendo un po’ serve, prendiamo dei gol troppo facili e questo non va bene, porta all’alternanza dei risultati. Rinforzi a gennaio? Pensare a quello che è successo e quello che sarà servito a poco. Vedremo cosa sarà. L’unica cosa che bisogna fare è andare in campo e giocare bene, la squadra ha fatfo buone partite in alcuni casi. Se prendiamo tutti quei gol negli ultimi trenta minuti vuol dire che non riusciamo a gestire alcuni momenti della partita. Non è questione di assenze, le assenze non sono una giustificazione. Dovrà essere una partita di sofferenza, siamo in tredici. Ci sarà da soffrire con una squadra che sta facendo molto bene. De Bruyne? Non è che non voglio dirlo, ma farà l’allenamento e manderò in campo chi sta in piedi”.

#2204. West Brom begin talks over new contract for £1.5m star

West Brom named George Campbell as their new club captain in the summer following a stellar debut campaign from the American defender. Signed for £1.5m from CF Montreal in 2025, he has emerged as a key player for WBA.

Now, the Baggies are looking to reward Campbell’s success with a new contract. Reporter Mike McGrath says on X that the club are in talks over a fresh deal for the 25-year-old, despite the fact he is already tied down until 2029 as it stands.

Prior to the summer transfer window, reports stated that Campbell had interest from Scottish giants Celtic, amongst other clubs. A new contract would further secure the American international’s future at The Hawthorns in case admiration from elsewhere grows.

Campbell had impressed in the MLS with CF Montreal after coming through the Atlanta United academy. He has made the step up to Championship football brilliantly, swiftly locking down a starting spot last term and growing in influence over time.

The Pennsylvania native spent the early days of his West Brom career playing at right-back, but shortly after his caretaker appointment, James Morrison moved Campbell into his regular central role and it brought instant results. In the final 11 games of last season, Campbell started all at centre-back and WBA were beaten just once, keeping seven clean sheets along the way.

The American provided some key attacking contributions too, scoring the Baggies’ only goals in draws against Charlton Athletic and Sheffield United, and in a win over Bristol City.

Campbell’s emergence as a key player saw his leadership traits shine through, earning him the captaincy in the summer. He has retained a big role in Albion’s success this term, contributing to the joint-tightest defence in the league with 13 goals conceded while ranking highly for successful passes (694 – top 5% of Championship centre-backs) and successful dribbles (eight – top 3%).

A new Campbell contract isn’t a must because of the time remaining on his existing deal. However, it will play a big part in keeping him happy and fending off potential admirers.

Improved terms reflect his value in the side as West Brom captain and a standout centre-back. It means that any potential admirers will have to part with a pretty penny to try and tempt him away from The Hawthorns.

His club success has brought more opportunities on the international stage, starting in two USMNT fixtures over the last break. As Campbell’s stock grows, WBA know they have to keep him happy if he’s to stay for the foreseeable.

#2202. James Penrice expecting '10 times’ the joy if Rangers lift Premier Sports Cup

James Penrice enjoyed Rangers’ Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Aberdeen but believes the winning feeling will multiply by 10 if they win the final.

The Light Blues registered a 1-0 victory at Barclays Hampden on Saturday thanks to a late but deserved goal from striker Ryan Naderi, who pounced on a strike towards goal from Penrice to direct the ball into the net from six yards.

Gers players took the acclaim of their fans at the end after confirming Derek McInnes’ first final as boss, with Rangers facing Hibernian at the national stadium on December 13 after the Hibees beat city rivals Hearts 2-1 on Sunday.

Penrice, on loan from Super League Greece side AEK Athens, said: “I think it’s special seeing boys that haven’t seen the kind of scenes before, haven’t seen Rangers at Hampden.

“I think it can only help. And I think it will be 10 times that if you were to come back here and win it in six weeks.

“So the motivation for the boys is to relive that again, 10 times that.

“And I think that’s what we’ll be trying to put into the group and it can only help us.”

Penrice admits his decision to join the Ibrox side in the summer was vindicated – albeit there had been no hesitation.

The former Partick Thistle, Livingston and Hearts left-back said: “It was never in doubt. Never.

“It was the only place I wanted to go in the summer. And I pushed a hell of a lot.

“This is why I want to come here and play for a massive club and play in games like a final. It only backs up my decision.”

It was not a classic display from Rangers, especially in a low-quality first half but Penrice stressed the importance of digging deep to get results.

He said: “I think that’s what it is. We’d love to be knocking the ball about and score six or seven goals, but sometimes that doesn’t happen.

“Teams come and they sit lower and they make it hard for us.

“At Rangers, that’s going to happen. You need to score goals. I think it’s just that final bit. The final pass, the final shot. I think composure in front of goal. But I can’t complain.

“The boys ran themselves into the ground and I think big Ryan gets his striker’s goal and it’s a massive positive.”

Although he had been pushed into midfield at times in previous games, Penrice started alongside Nico Raskin in the Gers engine room in a tactical move by McInnes which raised some eyebrows.

However, Penrice took it in his stride, saying: “It was obviously not what I’ve been used to in a two. But when the gaffer says play there, there’s no question, I’ll play wherever.

“Whatever I can do to help the team is what I’ll do.

“Obviously, it’s not a position I’ve played in before in the past for Livingstone and Partick.

“But if he asks me to play in there, I’m going to say yes. I could play anywhere.”

#2201. Simon Jordan drops 'crisis' claim as West Ham move to replace Nuno with Scott Parker

Former Crystal Palace chairman and talkSPORT pundit, Simon Jordan, has weighed in on the debate which has unsurprisingly surrounded West Ham United's decision to part ways with Nuno Espírito Santo.

The Hammers' former boss found himself under increasing pressure following Saturday's 3-1 loss against West Bromwich Albion at the London Stadium - a result which also made it successive home losses in the Championship for the pre-season title favourites.

Results elsewhere meant that the East London outfit had slipped down to eighth after 13 matches played, four points behind Swansea City, who occupy the final automatic promotion place ahead of the midweek round of fixtures.

Nuno opted to stay in E20 in the summer despite the intense speculation which surrounded his managerial position after West Ham were relegated from the Premier League for the first time in 14 years on the final day of last season.

The hierarchy at the London Stadium have swiftly turned their attention to sourcing a replacement, though, with it being widely reported that talks have reached an advanced stage for Scott Parker to take charge.

West Ham United have parted company with Portuguese head coach Nuno Espirito Santo and set their sights on Scott Parker

Nuno lasted just under 14 months in charge of West Ham, having taken over from Graham Potter last September following a disastrous start to last season.

Despite losing key names such as Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville this summer, it was largely expected that the 52-year-old would add to his previous Championship-winning term with Wolves, such is the quality that had remained at his disposal.

Nuno won 20 of his 53 matches in charge, but when asked for his thoughts on the club's major call by Jim White, Jordan said: "They're eighth in the league. Six points off top spot, which is not a catastrophe.

"It's not ideal for many sides. How did Ipswich get on last year when they got relegated? Were they setting the world alight when they first got down? I don't think they were. I think they were mid-table for significant parts of the season."

Jordan then continued his debate on whether moving for Parker, who was named the Football Writers' Association's Player of the Year in 2010/11 despite West Ham's relegation, is the right decision given his track record in the EFL and the Premier League.

"They've made a decision. Scott Parker has proven to be someone that's capable of getting teams out of the Championship. He's also proven to be someone that can't keep teams in the Premier League," stated Jordan.

"The aim, clearly, for West Ham, is to make decisions that get them out of the Championship as quickly as they possibly can because of the economics of it.

"Whether other people were involved in the decision. I should imagine David Sullivan is still a shareholder in West Ham, and whilst we're not seeing him front and centre anymore, I imagine he's got something to say about who the manager might be.

"With those things in mind, Scott Parker obviously played for West Ham. He will have a regard for the club, the club will have a regard for him," the pundit added. "He will do a job.

"But to be six points off top spot, 13 games into a season, doesn't feel like a crisis that would dictate the necessity to fire a manager, but that's what they've done."

#2200. Wrexham consider Welshman as potential Phil Parkinson replacement after Championship rival snub

Wrexham have risen from the National League to the Championship under Phil Parkinson‘s lead. But now, the boss is facing questions over his future, with the Red Dragons sat 18th in the table after only one win in their last five.

And, as the North Welsh side look to come good on their big ambitions, a managerial change may await. A report from talkSPORT states that Rob Edwards is among the contenders to take charge of Wrexham if they decide to part ways with Parkinson.

The Welshman recently rejected the chance to take charge of Burnley, who appointed Fabio Celestini instead. Edwards has been out of the game since he was sacked by Wolves in June, and he is now keen to return to the dugout.

Edwards has become a well-known manager over the past five years or so, first rising to prominence by leading Forest Green Rovers to the League Two title. A short and unsuccessful stint as Watford boss followed, but the 43-year-old succeeded in his next job by taking Luton Town to the Premier League in 2024.

He left Kenilworth Road as the Hatters struggled to get over the hangover of relegation from the top flight. Middlesbrough offered Edwards his return to the dugout in July 2025, and his impressive work with a PPG rate of 1.81 ultimately saw him poached by Wolves after only 16 matches.

Edwards’ return to Molineux – where he spent time as a player and coach – didn’t go as planned. Nevertheless, he remains held in high regard for his strong Championship record, often leading sides who utilise attack-minded wing-backs with intense and direct football.

This style of play will appeal to Wrexham, who have set up in a similar way on their journey through their leagues. Edwards has Championship success and Premier League experience under his belt though, unlike current boss Parkinson.

Moving on from Parkinson will not be easy for Wrexham when that day comes. The 58-year-old has led their rise from the fifth tier to Premier League contention, and he has regularly received the public backing of owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney.

However, as far as successors go, Edwards feels like a great fit. He has stronger pedigree to try and take the Red Dragons to the next level, yet his similar success with wing-backs means he might be able to get results with the current squad of players right off the bat.

Furthermore, his Welsh citizenship is sure to please supporters who will be happy to have a compatriot at the helm.

Time will tell if Parkinson can hold onto his position, but as pressure grows, Edwards could be an ideal heir.

#2198. Harry Redknapp fires warning to West Ham fans over Scott Parker appointment

Former West Ham player and manager Harry Redknapp has warned Hammers supporters that they may have to see an unattractive brand of football under Scott Parker due to the limitations of the playing squad.

The East London outfit sacked Nuno Espírito Santo on Tuesday morning following successive home defeats to Southampton and West Brom, which has left the Hammers eighth in the Championship table before their trip to Cardiff City on Wednesday evening.

The hierarchy have moved swiftly to find his successor, with former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker set to land the role.

Parker has guided all of Bournemouth, Fulham and Burnley back to the promised land, with his excellent CV in the second tier enough to convince those at the top of West Ham that he can register a fourth promotion at the London Stadium.

Questions have been raised about whether Parker is a long-term fit for the club should he get them back to the top-flight, but focus for now remains on getting the Hammers back towards the top end of the table, with the team’s confidence bound to have been dented after successive home defeats against fellow promotion rivals.

Meanwhile, Harry Redknapp, who has such a deep connection to West Ham after coming through the youth ranks as a player and going on to eventually manage the club, has commented on Parker being close to landing the job, and what the supporters can expect from him in the dugout.

Before a ball was kicked ahead of the new Championship season, many were touting West Ham to run away with the division and be convincing champions, in turn sealing an instant return to the Premier League.

But it’s been far from straight forward, with Hammers supporters deeply frustrated by the performances during their opening 13 games.

Fans have been worried for a while about the style of play and the team’s inability to start games quickly enough, and those problems came to roost against two promotion rivals in Southampton and West Brom over the last week, who put West Ham to the sword in front of their own supporters.

Such heavy defeats dropped West Ham to eighth in the table, which was enough to make the hierarchy believe that Nuno was not the man to lead the club forward.

The club confirmed his departure on their club website, which read: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team Head Coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the Board of Directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant Head Coach Rui Pedro Silva and Goalkeeper Coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new Head Coach is already underway.

“Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the Club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new Head Coach is confirmed.”

In the next few hours, a report by the BBC revealed that West Ham were in advanced talks to name Scott Parker as Nuno’s successor, and that his appointment could be confirmed before Wednesday's Championship clash against the Bluebirds.

Speaking to Jeff Stelling and Andy Townsend live on TalkSPORT (From 11:35), Harry Redknapp, who managed 322 games for West Ham between 1994 and 2001, reacted to the developing news of Scott Parker closing in on the Hammers job.

And he fired over a warning to the fanbase about expectations over the style of play under Parker, acknowledging that while the supporters want to see an entertaining way of playing, the limitations in the playing squad may make it difficult for Parker to deliver such a front-footed approach.

Responding to Townsend’s question about Parker striking the right balance, Redknapp replied: “They want to see you play football for sure, if you can, but as you know, Andy, you need players that can play to play good football. They can all come in and have ideas about what we should be doing.

“West Ham was called the academy because they had incredible players like Jonny Burn, Alan Devonshire, (Tony) Cottie, (Frank) McAvennie, Billy Bonds, Frank Lampard, you go back to Bobby Moore, Geoff Hurst, Martin Peters, they’ve had incredible players, they haven’t got them players now, so whatever it takes to get out the division, then that’s what Scott’s got to really.

“If it means playing up to a big centre-forward and getting up the park, then that’s what you’ve got to do.

“They can all dream of a philosophy, but it’s not easy to implement unless you’ve got the players.”

Reaction to the news of Nuno Espírito Santo departing the London Stadium was largely positive, but there have been some mixed views about Scott Parker stepping into the hotseat.

Dave from West Ham TV is a fan of Parker coming in for the short-term, but believes in the long-term he will end up failing.

Dorset Hammer has shown some concern about the short amount of time Parker has stayed at clubs during his managerial career so far, pointing out that he hasn’t lasted longer than 18 months at any of his former employers.

West Ham fan Nathan is also not a fan of the Parker appointment, believing Kieran McKenna was a better and at the same time, still a realistic target.

Finally, another Hammers fan has backed Parker to come into the club and get them promoted, but says the club should then part ways given his poor track record in the top-flight.

There is gigantic pressure and expectation awaiting Scott Parker, and given the mixed reviews on social media to his arrival, it doesn’t appear his extensive time as a Hammers player will grant him much patience.

West Ham have to turn the tide quickly if they are to avoid slipping down the table further, as if that happens, there could be an increase of swirling toxicity that makes Parker’s job so much harder to succeed in.

There’s a lot of areas to fix for Parker, with organisation in the backline a priority, which has been on show with the Hammers conceding six goals in their last two home matches.

West Ham fans, do you back Scott Parker to turn the tide at the London Stadium? Can he be a long-term replacement for Nuno? Drop your thoughts in the comments below!

It may have to see Parker batten down the hatches and start grinding out results, although that is something that could grate with the supporters given their urge to see a positive style of play.

But what matters most is getting back to the Premier League. If the results turn because of the change, then many can’t complain, but if the style of play gets worse and the results don’t improve, then Parker may not be in his post for too long.

It’s such a big job for Parker to take on, with his credibility as a boss on the line following on from yet another short last stint at Turf Moor.

#2197. Celtic Fans Collective demand Dermot Desmond attend AGM in person and face scrutiny

Celtic Fans Collective have called on Dermot Desmond to attend the upcoming Celtic AGM in person.

The supporter group issued a lengthy statement demanding that the Parkhead shareholder show up to the event in person to face scrutiny over boardroom decisions.

The group claims Desmond wields "considerable influence over the direction and decision-making" at the club and must "answer questions about his role".

A Celtic Fans Collective statement read: "For twenty years, Dermot Desmond has not attended Celtic's Annual General Meeting, despite wielding considerable influence over the direction and decision-making of our club.

"Although only a minority shareholder, Desmond appears to exercise influence far beyond his shareholding. With that influence comes a responsibility to be accountable.

"We call on Dermot Desmond to publicly commit to attending the 2026 AGM in person and answer questions about his role in the running of Celtic Football Club.

"Sending his son, another representative or a prepared statement in his place is no substitute for attending personally.

"The decision by Peter Lawwell to prematurely conclude last year's AGM left a clear impression among supporters that the Board had taken an opportunity to avoid scrutiny. Responsibility for how that meeting was conducted and ultimately concluded rests entirely with the Board.

"This year, however, the focus must be firmly on scrutiny rather than protest. There is a clear understanding across the support that the AGM must provide the opportunity for important questions to be put directly to those running the Club, without allowing scrutiny to be evaded once again.

"Celtic supporters have repeatedly sought meaningful dialogue and a more constructive relationship with the Club.

"At a time when fans want to see decisive leadership, a public commitment from Dermot Desmond to attend the AGM in good faith would be an important demonstration of his willingness to engage directly with supporters and shareholders."

Celtic Trust added: "As a Non-Executive Director of the Club, it is the duty of Dermot Desmond to attend the 2026 Celtic PLC AGM.

"He has been absent from these meetings for 20 years - refusing to face and answer questions from shareholders.

"He should commit to ending that absence this year."

#2195. Kim Hellberg drops new Will Lankshear update in big Middlesbrough boost

Kim Hellberg has eased fears regarding a potential injury issue at Middlesbrough for star striker Will Lankshear.

The forward has been a stunning addition to the Teesside outfit from Tottenham Hotspur over the summer, making a big splash in these opening months of the new Championship season.

The 21-year-old found the back of the net on the 12th and 13th occasions of the campaign in the team’s 3-0 victory against Charlton Athletic last weekend.

However, he was substituted in the closing stages, and was seen limping off the field, which raised worries among supporters that he could be facing an absence through injury.

Lankshear arrived from Spurs in a deal worth a total value of £20 million, with the club hoping he can play a role in helping the team gain promotion to the Premier League.

Hellberg’s side lost the play-off final last May, but their positive form in the first 13 rounds of this season have them in the mix for a top two position so far.

Speaking ahead of Middlesbrough’s upcoming clash away to Wrexham, Hellberg assured supporters that Lankshear’s withdrawal was just due to cramp.

According to journalist Dom Shaw, the Boro boss confirmed that the forward was taken off with the issue, and he should be available again midweek.

Southampton and Middlesbrough were set to be handed blows in January - but not anymore

However, Rokas Pukstas will be absent for at least another month, with no specific timeframe given for his potential return to fitness.

The midfielder arrived at the Riverside in the summer from Hajduk Split, but has only made one appearance in the Championship.

He came off the bench in the 1-0 win against QPR in September, but has been unavailable for selection due to a hamstring injury suffered in training in October.

Alfie Jones is the only other absence, with the defender still recovering from a calf issue.

Middlesbrough are currently top of the Championship table after the opening 13 games, with the team earning 28 points.

Hellberg’s side are two points clear of Swansea City in second, and another two clear of third place Wolves, as they target a top two finish in the league.

Boro have lost just once, and are unbeaten since their 2-1 defeat to Blackburn Rovers on 22 August, going 11 without a loss.

Next up for Middlesbrough is a trip to face Wrexham on Wednesday evening in a 7.45pm kick-off.

Lankshear has been sensational this season, and his brace at the weekend was yet another reminder of his importance to the club already.

So fans are going to be extra wary of any signs of a possible injury because of how significant his form has been.

It’s a positive sign for Wednesday night that he should be fit and ready to go, although it’s becoming apparent that he can’t quite manage 90 minutes every game.

It wouldn’t be a surprise that he only features for some of this clash against the Red Dragons, but being able to get him in from the start will be a relief for supporters.

#2194. Will Lankshear set for England audition as Thomas Tuchel’s scouts prepare for Middlesbrough trip

Middlesbrough signed Will Lankshear in a deal potentially worth up to £20m in the summer, and the striker has been one of the Championship’s stars of the season so far. The 21-year-old’s return of 15 goals in 16 Boro games has raised questions over a potential call-up to the England senior squad.

Now, a report from talkSPORT states that Thomas Tuchel is keeping a keen eye on Lankshear, and scouts are set to watch the striker in action when Middlesbrough face Wrexham on Wednesday night. The Boro star will be looking to score in a sixth consecutive league match.

Tuchel’s next England squad will be named on Friday as UEFA Nations League games against Spain and Croatia approach.

It is a real rarity for Championship players to earn call-ups to the England squad. The last player to be capped by the Three Lions while at a second-tier club was Sam Johnstone in 2021, with Wilfried Zaha, David Nugent, Jay Bothroyd and Jack Butland among other past examples.

Middlesbrough man Lankshear has been a regular in the Young Lions setup, picking up caps at U19, U20 and U21 levels over the past three years.

There can be no denial of Lankshear’s form – 15 goals puts him clear of all other English strikers, including new Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. He heads into the Wrexham game off the back of back-to-back braces and he leads the way in the Championship for goals, xG, non-penalty xG, shots and shots on target (Fotmob).

It comes down to the competition for a place, with the last England squad containing captain Kane and Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the only natural strikers. Ivan Toney has 14 goals in 15 games over in Saudi Arabia this season, while Ollie Watkins has six goals in 10 games in the Middle East too.

English strikers Dominic Solanke and Liam Delap have struggled for Premier League form and seem unlikely to come into contention.

If Tuchel would prefer to pick a domestically-based player over Toney or Watkins, Lankshear is arguably the third-best option behind Kane and Calvert-Lewin. It would be a huge step for the Boro star, but it is certainly feasible that he earns a call.

At only 21, Lankshear is emerging as one of England’s brightest young prospects. The Middlesbrough man has already drawn comparisons to Harry Kane, and his form in front of goal is scintillating.

The most exciting thing is that, at his young age, the best is yet to come from Lankshear. It means that while there is a case for him to be called up for the next England internationals, it is not the end of the world if Tuchel overlooks him for now.

Lankshear will be widely backed to make the jump some day. His form means he has a better chance than any of his recent Championship compatriots, but Tuchel is yet to call up someone from England’s second tier, so he may opt to wait until the Boro star has experience at a higher level.

#2193. Fresh Oldham Athletic development sparks fierce backlash online

Oldham Athletic have had their appeals against Kai Payne and Kane Drummond's red cards in Saturday's defeat to Crawley Town rejected, which has not gone down well with the Latics fanbase.

Despite being tipped as one of the potential promotion contenders, it has been a poor start to the season for Oldham in League Two, and it was another frustrating afternoon for Micky Mellon's men against Crawley on Saturday.

Oldham had won just one of their previous nine league games prior to Saturday's meeting with bottom side Crawley, and their dismal form continued as they slumped to a 1-0 defeat to the Red Devils at Boundary Park, but the scoreline alone does not tell the full story of the dramatic encounter.

The Latics were reduced to 10 men in the 14th minute when Payne was sent off for a challenge on Danilo Orsi, and their afternoon went from bad to worse when Hammond saw red for a high boot on Kai Jennings just 16 minutes later.

Oldham battled valiantly despite their numerical disadvantage, but Crawley took the lead in the 52nd minute when Orsi bundled the ball home from close range after Charlie Barker to hit the crossbar, and they held on for just their second victory of the season.

The Latics currently sit 21st in the League Two table, and they are only outside the relegation zone on goal difference, but they have a chance to pull clear of danger when they face fellow strugglers Northampton Town at Sixfields on Tuesday night.

With many feeling that Payne and Drummond's red cards were harsh, Oldham submitted appeals against the decisions in an attempt to get their suspensions overturned, but it was confirmed on Tuesday that both had been rejected.

That means that Payne and Drummond will be unavailable for the game at Northampton on Tuesday night, as well as Sunday's FA Cup tie against League One side Sheffield Wednesday at Boundary Park and next Saturday's trip to Shrewsbury Town.

After returning for a third loan spell with the Latics this summer, Payne has scored one goal in eight appearances so far this season, while Drummond has netted two goals and provided one assist in 16 appearances.

However, Mellon will now be without the pair for three of the next four games, although they will be able to feature in next Tuesday's EFL Trophy clash at Barnsley as suspensions from the league do not carry over to that competition.

Oldham are not the only club to have failed in an appeal against a double red card in recent weeks, with National League side Carlisle United also having their appeals against Miguel Azeez and Harvey Bunker's dismissals in their 3-0 win over Harrogate Town last month turned down.

With plenty of Oldham supporters still feeling angry about the refereeing decisions in Saturday's defeat to Crawley, it is fair to say that the news that the appeals against Payne and Drummond's red cards had been rejected was not well-received, with many taking to social media to vent their fury in response to the club's announcement on X.

The incidents continued Oldham's long-standing frustration with referee David Rock, who sent off two Latics players last season, Ryan Woods and Mike Fondop, with the latter's red card later being rescinded after a successful appeal.

Greater Manchester Police are currently investigating after video footage emerged appearing to show a fan throwing a crutch towards Rock as he was walking towards the tunnel, and Oldham supporters seem in no mood to forgive the official for his latest questionable calls.

After their appeals were rejected, there is nothing more the Latics can do to reverse Payne and Drummond's red cards, but one supporter called for Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is known to be a passionate Everton fan, to intervene.

#2192. The curious case of Joe Aribo as Rangers hero triggers comeback from football exile

Former Rangers hero Joe Aribo has been without a club since leaving Southampton in the summer following a loan spell at Leicester City.

It's a curious case for the former Ibrox maverick. Devastatingly effective on his day, yet clubless at the age of 30.

But Aribo is doing the opposite of giving in. He is currently putting in the hard yards in Dubai as he aims to reignite his career.

The midfielder's versatility was one of his greatest strengths, as he demonstrated by starting and scoring in the Europa League Final against Eintracht Frankfurt in Seville while operating as a makeshift false nine.

Aribo thrilled supporters during his time in Glasgow and went on to become an important player for Southampton, making 111 appearances for the Saints and sampling life in the Premier League.

Steven Gerrard adored him and Giovanni van Bronckhorst could scarcely do without him.

Now, however, Aribo finds himself on the outside looking in after the most frustrating period of his career.

Read more: Celtic supporter group demand Dermot Desmond end 20-year absence and attend AGM

Game time proved hard to come by at Southampton under Tonda Eckert and an ill-fated loan move to Leicester did little to improve matters. Minutes were scarce at the King Power and relegation only added to the disappointment.

For a player who once dazzled on European nights and played a leading role in one of Rangers' greatest modern runs, it has been a sobering fall from grace.

But the Nigeria international is now rested, recharged and desperate for another opportunity to prove he can still perform at the highest level.

The hard work is being done behind the scenes. Now Aribo is simply waiting on the chance to remind everyone why he was once one of the most coveted talents in Scottish football.

#2191. West Brom set for major boost - it will impact Celtic

West Bromwich Albion are plotting fresh contract action to secure the long-term future and reward the performances of a star performer at the Hawthorns in a new development which could have a detrimental transfer impact for Scottish giants Celtic.

The Baggies have undertaken serious strides in what represents James Morrison's first full campaign in charge, with the ex-Albion midfield star having guided his old side to safety in the dying embers of the previous campaign before directing a play-off charge this time around.

West Brom find themselves positioned fourth in the Championship ahead of this evening's crunch home clash against promotion rivals Southampton following three victories in their last four matches over Wrexham, Blackburn Rovers and title favourites West Ham.

An uplifting summer transfer window enabled supporters to dream of promotion pushes once again, and the Baggies did well to bolster Morrison's squad with influential signings such as Felix Horn Myhre, Jimmy-Jay Morgan and Rabby Nzingoula while retaining star performers in the Black Country.

It's no secret that a number of West Brom's players did attract interest, and one of those players to have earned admirers elsewhere is now edging closer to extending his stay in blue-and-white in what will come as a blow as far as Celtic are concerned.

The player in question is skipper George Campbell, who, as per a new update via X from Mike McGrath of the Telegraph, has been sought out for a contract extension by Albion.

Just this afternoon, McGrath has reported that West Brom have entered negotiations over a new contract for Campbell in an effort to reflect the three-cap USMNT international's ever-growing importance and authority at the Hawthorns after initially arriving in the summer of 2025 in a £1.5 million deal from MLS outfit CF Montreal.

Campbell enjoyed a positive individual debut campaign last time out in spite of West Brom's collective struggles, which would see the defender earn wide plaudits for his steely and composed defensive displays while racking up 39 Championship appearances and finding the back of the net on four occasions.

After being named as West Brom's club captain over the summer following Jed Wallace's departure, Campbell has taken his performances up a notch and has relished the added responsibility as the heartbeat of a much-sturdier backline under Morrison.

These five players won't be available when these two early pace-setters battle at the Hawthorns

That's exactly why the Black Country outfit are now pushing to secure a new contract for Campbell, who has appeared in all but one of his side's second-tier fixtures to date, and still has just under three years remaining on his current terms.

West Brom's ongoing contract negotiations with Campbell will represent a considerable boost to all at the Hawthorns if such discussions come to fruition, providing the Baggies with fresh security in the transfer market and protecting one of their prised assets from being poached while rewarding the 25-year-old with the sort of deal that his ever-increasing importance has only warranted.

It's not quite so much a boost for Celtic, however, with Martin O'Neill's side having reportedly expressed an interest in the ex-Atlanta United ace's signature at the back-end of the 2025/26 term.

Reports had suggested that Celtic were interested in Campbell alongside unnamed Bundesliga and Championship clubs, even indicating that the then-£2.5 million-rated Albion defender was open to the possibility of a switch to Parkhead.

It never materialised, though, and Celtic would actually last the summer transfer window without acquiring a central defender as O'Neill only made minor adjustments to his backline.

Naturally, West Brom supporters are excited by the news that a new contract for Campbell could be nearing.

#2189. Hibs' astonishing 47-year Hampden record vs Rangers sets up classic

Hibernian head into next month's Premier Sports Cup Final against Rangers with their tails up.

Granted the club's Scottish Premiership form leaves plenty to be desired, but their semi-final victory over fierce rivals Hearts on Sunday afternoon highlighted the fighting spirit still within the camp.

Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath's goals cancelled out Claudio Braga's early opener and set up the showpiece finale at Hampden Park on December 13. And it turns out Hibs have more to be excited and confident about given their history against the Light Blues at the national stadium.

Marink Reedijk's squad will square off against Derek McInnes' charges and they will do so with the bit between their teeth in the competition. But they also have history on their side.

Hibs have astonishingly not been beaten by Rangers at Hampden in a whopping 47 years.

The last time the Glasgow outfit came out on top was at the 1979 Scottish Cup final which took three attempts following a goalless draw in the initial final and then another in the replay. Rangers would win the third contest 3-2.

Since that period the two clubs have faced off four more times at Hampden and the Leith side have come out on top each time.

First came in the League Cup semi-final of 1991 when Keith Wright netted the winner inside the first 30 minutes. Then in 2004 Hibs progressed to the final of the same competition with a penalty shootout victory over their opponents following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Stephen Dobbie had levelled after Michael Mols had opened the scoring for Gers during normal time.

The iconic 2016 Scottish Cup Final was next when former defender and then head coach David Gray bulleted home the winning header after an exhausting 3-2 victory for Hibs.

And in 2021 Hibs continued their reign of Hampden dominance over Rangers when they knocked them out of the League Cup at the semi-final stage again. Boyle fired in a stunning first-half hattrick before Scott Arfield nicked a consolation.

It's a staggering statistic and one Hibs will be desperate to add to when the final rolls around next month.
