#2043. Expert mystified by what he saw from James Trafford at Leeds

Leeds United were asking for trouble by attempting to play out from the back against Bournemouth on Saturday.

That is the opinion of experienced former Tottenham, Aston Villa and Everton scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Whites were beaten courtesy of goals from Evanilson and Amine Adli, with the former given an absolute gift by James Trafford.

The England international had the ball inside the box and looked to find Ao Tanaka, who was caught on his heels completely by Justin Kluivert.

The Dutchman simply slid the ball across for Evanilson to poke into an empty net, handing Bournemouth the lead and eventually the three points.

Trafford, 24, joined Leeds from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £45million in the summer transfer window, and had been enjoying a good start.

📰 Defeat in Bournemouth. pic.twitter.com/5ArBkOrCi6

Trafford is not prone to mistakes with the ball at his feet, and his ability to pass was undoubtedly considered when Leeds signed him.

If they get it right, passing out from the back can get a team into great positions beyond their opponent's midfield.

But get it wrong, and the consequences can be brutal - as Leeds learned on Saturday.

"That's another thing I don't understand, is the goal kicks from the six yard, it's just awful," King told Football Insider.

"You play it to somebody ten yards from goal, he plays it back, he plays it left, he plays it back to the keeper, he plays it out right, comes to the centre half - they've had ten passes and the ball's only just got out of the penalty area.

"Now, if you're going to press, then that's the easy way you can press teams. Just get the ball, get the ball up and look to win the second one.

"Get it wide, get it in. You saw the way Arsenal done it, they got it forward, got it back, got it in and scored.

"That's football. But all this pitter-pattering around in your own box, why encourage teams to put you under pressure?"

Not only Trafford, but several Premier League goalkeepers had a weekend to forget.

Zion Suzuki, who has been excellent for Aston Villa, dropped a corner into his own net against Fulham.

And even the most experienced were at it. Alisson's wayward pass was cut out by Martin Odegaard in the build up to Kai Havertz's winner on Sunday.

Goalkeeping is often a thankless task, but it is about how you bounce back from the errors.

#2042. ‘It affected my family’ – VAR official reveals full impact of huge decision which cost Liverpool

The official who was on VAR duty for the wrongly disallowed Luis Diaz goal in Liverpool’s 2-1 defeat to Tottenham in 2023 has spoken about the impact that the controversy had on his family.

The Colombian thought he had put the Reds 1-0 up in the 35th minute of the game in north London, but he was incorrectly flagged for offside, and a subsequent review from Stockley Park saw that erroneous decision upheld.

When the audio from the VAR conversation was publicly released a few days later, it was revealed that Darren England – the official on duty – had given the message of ‘check complete’ to the on-field referee in the mistaken belief that the goal was allowed to stand.

The 40-year-old has given an interview to BBC Sport in which he reflected on the regret from that hugely controversial decision, and how the fallout seeped into his family life.

England recalled: “Once I realised I’d made the error, it’s a really difficult place to try to forget that and move on. I can’t just physically stand up and walk out and leave it alone. A lot of resilience was needed – a lot of experience as well.”

He added: “The aftermath obviously was really difficult to deal with. It was challenging because it’s the goldfish bowl of the Premier League, but when mistakes happen, then you’re in the public eye and criticism’s inevitably going to come your way.

“That was difficult because it affected my family as well. We had people outside my girls’ school, journalists and things like that. That then affects you not as a referee, but as a human being.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The catalogue of errors which led to Diaz’s legitimate goal being disallowed was farcical, with all of the officials on duty collectively culpable for the shambolic process which unfolded.

England did acknowledge in the VAR audio that he thought the on-field decision was onside and immediately held his hands up to the error, but that came as no comfort to anyone associated with Liverpool after such a costly and preventable outcome.

🚨 OFFICIAL: PGMOL have released VAR audio from Spurs v Liverpool 🔊 pic.twitter.com/zNLDyHkBbe

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 3, 2023

Criticism of the officials botching the process was inevitable and justified, but obviously the media intrusion into the referee’s family life crossed an unacceptable line, and we can empathise with how difficult the fallout must’ve been for the now 40-year-old.

Unfortunately, more than three years on from that chaotic blunder, refereeing standards in the Premier League haven’t improved to any great extent, as we saw at the weekend with the inexplicable decision not to award a penalty for a clear pull by Jurrien Timber on Alexander Isak’s shirt.

Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb needs to do much more to ensure that a satisfactory standard of officiating is reached, but no person deserves to have an error in the course of the work turn into an unwarranted invasion on their family life.

Andrey Santos made a bright first Manchester United appearance as they fell to a pre-season friendly loss to Wrexham in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal with an easy finish six minutes before half-time, moments after heading against his own crossbar defending a corner.

United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Moments later Smith was on the scoresheet at the other end and it looked all too easy as he was left with a tap-in after O’Brien’s cross appeared to go through Harry Maguire’s legs.

United dominated the ball but struggled to fashion chances as the pace of the game dropped. Instead, Wrexham threatened with a low shot from Davis Keillor-Dunn but Radek Vitek made the save.

When Ethan Wheatley prodded Harry Amass’ cross goalwards in the 78th minute, it was their first shot on target, but Dan Ward made the save before holding a low drive from Shea Lacey.

Dan Gore hit the deck in the single minute of stoppage time, but his optimistic penalty appeal was waved away.

Man Utd appeal unsuccessfully for a penalty when Dan Gore goes over in the area. Seconds later, the referee blows the final whistle. Wrexham, who were under pressure for much of the second half, have held on to beat Manchester United in a muted pre-season friendly in Helsinki.

Sam Smith scored the only goal in the 39th minute, having headed against his own crossbar three minutes earlier. There were 21 changes at half-time, 11 for Man Utd and 10 for Wrexham.

Andrey Santos, part of an experienced first-half XI, had a decent debut after signing from Chelsea in the week. Wheatley finds the underlapping Amass, whose pullback is cleared a little desperately by Wrexham. Amass, still only 19, looks really promising at left-back.

No attempts at goal in the second half, on or off target, from either team. But the young Man Utd side have played some purposeful stuff and have had around 66% possession.

No chances to report but the young Man Utd side have started well, dominating possession and playing with greater urgency than their elders.

39 min: Man Utd 0 Wrexham 1 (Smith) Sam Smith gives Wrexham the lead. It came from a well-worked throw-in on the left. Thomason played a one-two before slipping a crisp pass into O’Brien in the area. His precise low cross, through the legs of Maguire, gave Smith a tap-in from three yards.

Youri Tielemans is targeting more silverware after completing his £35m move to Manchester United.

“The ambition from everyone at the club is extremely clear; we are all determined to push for the biggest trophies,” he said.

#2039. GdS: Ten-point risk and high ambitions – three keys for Amorim in Milan-Inter

AC Milan are taking on their city rivals Inter this morning, and for Ruben Amorim, there is one key player in each department.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Milan are entering the derby at a pretty clear disadvantage, currently seven points behind Inter in the standings. Ruben Amorim made it clear yesterday that the Scudetto remains the goal, but if the gap is increased to ten, it will be tough.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s true that Stefano Pioli, in February 2022, also risked going ten points behind until Olivier Giroud turned the game around. The problem is that his successor Goncalo Ramos hasn’t even scored a goal in the league since the end of August.

Furthermore, Cristian Chivu and his Inter have been in very good form lately and will be looking to end their seven-game run without a win in the fixture. It’s going to be a night with a lot of emotions, so let’s see how it will pan out on the pitch.

Mario Gila’s return is absolutely essential for Milan, but it will take more from them to regain solidity at the back. The Rossoneri have conceded four more goals than they did at this point last season, and six in their last two home games.

Switching from Max Allegri’s low block to Amorim’s more proactive style of play has clearly come with a cost. Yet, it’s not like the Rossoneri have been pressing like crazy so far, which is obvious when you compare them with Inter.

The Nerazzurri have a much higher centre of gravity (54.7-48.5 m), they steal more balls in the final third of the pitch (41-28), and they shoot more from offensive recoveries (13-7). Meanwhile, Milan are continuing to concentrate, play vertically and run quickly.

There is also another truth that needs to be highlighted: too many goals have been conceded due to individual errors. Amorim is well aware of this and it might have something to do with the decision to start Sankhoun Diawara on the left, with effectively four centre-backs in the back four.

In midfield, just like with Gila in defence, Amorim can count on another crucial return: Adrien Rabiot, the team’s top scorer along with Alphadjo Cisse (4 goals). For Milan, the midfielders are crucial with their goals.

The midfield is indeed the centre of Milan’s power, where the Ballon d’Or winner Luka Modric reigns supreme and where counterattacks that end up in goal are born. Amorim’s choices in this department weren’t easy.

The most tested on the eve of the match: a 4-3-3 with Musah and Rabiot on either side of Modric, and an attacking trident of Moreira-Ramos-Pulisic.

There were fewer doubts for Chivu who has a tested midfield and, in general, the most coherent team in the league. But that doesn’t mean they don’t have problems. Against Venezia, Inter suffered six dangerous transitions, against Roma there were seven.

In the middle of the pitch, due to the pressure of pressing or laziness in the return, there have often been gaps to exploit. It’s extremely dangerous to leave that space against galloping players like Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic, and Rabiot.

The Frenchman, who already crippled Inter on the counterattack as a Juventus player (goal and assist for Kostic), could become a key factor in the derby.

Despite conceding one fewer goal than a year ago (10-11), as the pink newspaper continues, Inter appear to be more vulnerable at the back. The centre-backs have dipped in form and the conceded xG is much higher, which Milan will try to exploit.

Ramos is pushing hard to score his third league goal, which he desperately needs despite adding a lot to Milan’s game: 14 balls recovered (Thuram 4, Lautaro 5, Pio 8), 21 lay-offs (Thuram 7, Lautaro 8, Pio 13). All he has to do is find the net.

However, if the player that Milan fear the most is Thuram, then that player is Pulisic for Inter. He decided the penultimate derby, scored in the one that stopped the haemorrhage of six defeats, and also impressed in the Supercoppa Italiana.

He knows the art of hiding between the lines and striking from the attacking midfield, which Inter’s 3-5-2 often struggles to achieve. Perhaps he can celebrate his contract renewal by deciding yet another derby.

Liverpool intend to sell midfielder Harvey Elliott in January if Valencia terminate his loan spell, sources have told Football Insider.

The La Liga side are searching for a way to bring the loan deal to a premature close, with the 23-year-old still yet to start a game for them.

There is a growing expectation that he will be sent back to Anfield in January, which sources say would effectively set him back to "square one."

Liverpool are understood to see no long-term future for Elliott on Merseyside, and would look to cash in ahead of his contract expiring in 2028.

The young midfielder has struggled to make any sort of impact for Valencia, playing just 152 minutes of La Liga action so far this season.

He is also currently serving a suspension after he was sent off for dissent in the dying embers of the recent defeat to Villarreal.

Elliott endured a hugely difficult loan spell with Aston Villa last term, and he is being faced by serious issues once again in 2026-27.

The English starlet was taken to Valencia by former West Brom manager Carlos Corberan, but he and ex-chief executive Ron Gourlay have since departed the club.

The managerial change has seen Javier Aguirre take the reins, but that has done little to change Elliott's situation.

With Valencia struggling in the relegation zone in La Liga, they are hoping to take Elliott off their wage bill this winter and send him back to Anfield.

However, the Reds have already made it clear that there is no way back for him at his parent club, given how far he is down the pecking order.

As a result, a permanent exit from Liverpool is the only option for the youngster if he is unable to turn his fortunes at Valencia around.

However, sources say that Monaco still require a big-name sale this winter in order to balance their books, with Camara their primary candidate to be moved on.

That looks set to play right into Liverpool's hands, as the Senegal international is towards the top of their list of targets to bolster their midfield.

#2037. One thing Italy boss Roberto Mancini did recently shows exactly what he thinks of Giovanni Leoni

Giovanni Leoni appears to be firmly in the mind of Italy head coach Roberto Mancini, judging by one recent report from his homeland.

The Liverpool defender has been out injured for more than a year after rupturing his ACL on his debut for the Reds against Southampton in September 2025, with the 19-year-old since undergoing a lengthy road to recovery.

Despite some hopes that he’d resume team training during the most recent international window a month ago, Andoni Iraola has since indicated that such a step will hopefully be taken during the upcoming round of national team fixtures in mid-November.

Even though Leoni hasn’t played a match of any description for more than 13 months, it seems that he hasn’t been forgotten by Mancini.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, the Italy head coach travelled to England in the hope of seeing the Liverpool defender (among several other candidates for Azzurri selection) on the pitch, but the teenager hadn’t recovered in time for the 61-year-old’s visit.

The report stated that the Reds’ number 15 ‘may return after the international break’, although that didn’t specify whether it’d be in the form of team training or clearance to finally resume playing.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Even with Leoni sidelined for so long, that Mancini reportedly wanted to see him in action on his vist to England attests to how highly the Italy boss regards the Liverpool defender.

The heartbreaking ACL injury overshadowed just how well the centre-back played on his Reds debut against Southampton before the cruellest intervention of fate, and the ex-Manchester City manager clearly has plenty of faith in the 19-year-old’s abilities.

The day that the young Italian is finally back in action will be one to cherish, although it’ll naturally take him time to get back into the rhythm of playing after being ruled out for 13 months and counting.

He could also have a difficult task on his hands trying to break up the uncompromising centre-back partnership of Virgil van Dijk and Jeremy Jacquet, with the latter particularly excelling since coming to Liverpool from Rennes in the summer.

Right now, though, simply getting back on the pitch will represent a seminal moment for Leoni, who should be given a tremendous boost by knowing that Mancini has him in his plans for the Italy squad.

#2036. Man United transfer news: £45m Bruno Fernandes 'uncertainty' hanging over January window as Michael Carrick considers sale

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 19:13

Al-Hilal are considering returning with €55m (£45.82m) offer for Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes in January, the latest report has claimed.

The Red Devils' turbulent season shows no signs of slowing down following their 2-0 defeat against Chelsea on Saturday.

Michael Carrick's woes in the Premier League have left them in 17th place with just seven points, and there have been several reasons for their poor form.

Attacker Fernandes have been blamed for not only his inconsistent displays, but also his conduct as the team's captain, so it is no surprise to see links re-emerge to the Saudi Pro League once again.

Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal have previously been credited with interest in the Portuguese international, and a report from Tuttomercatoweb claims that they are willing to offer as much as €55m (£45.82m) to land him.

There is no doubt that Fernandes has been the best signing for the Red Devils since the retirement of Sir Alex Ferguson in 2013.

However, questions have to be asked about his long-term future now that he is 32, especially as he has showed some signs of decline.

In 12 games for United this term, the captain has scored four goals and provided one assist, though three goals and ]one assist came in a 5-2 win against Ipswich Town on August 30.

Fernandes has often been reckless with his pressing, and perhaps his exit in January would benefit the team's ability to control matches.

Losing Fernandes would rob the team of their main creative spark, but there is an argument that becoming stronger defensively must be seen as the club's priority.

Any funds from the captain's exit should be used to sign at least one defender considering Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire have often been at the crime scene this season, watching United concede 24 goals in 13 matches.

While United may play less bravely should Fernandes exit, taking fewer risks could help them stave off the threat of relegation.

#2035. ‘Hopefully…’ – Andoni Iraola hints at potential Ryan Gravenberch return date after injury blow

Andoni Iraola has provided an update on the injury which has ruled Ryan Gravenberch out of Liverpool’s Champions League fixture against Fenerbahce.

The Merseyside club confirmed on Tuesday morning that the midfielder hasn’t travelled with the rest of the squad for the game in Istanbul tomorrow due to a heel injury and will instead undergo recovery at the AXA Training Centre.

While that obviously comes as a body blow for the Reds for the match against Dirk Kuyt’s side, it appears that the 24-year-old is unlikely to be sidelined for long.

Iraola was prompted for an update on Gravenberch during his pre-match press conference in Istanbul this afternoon, and the Liverpool head coach is hopeful that the Dutchman will be cleared to resume playing quickly.

The Reds boss said (via Liverpool Echo): “It’s a day-to-day thing. It’s a heel injury. He’s had some discomfort. He was warming up against Arsenal and was not 100%. Hopefully he can be available for the weekend, but we cannot say for sure.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

If Iraola has left the door open for Gravenberch to potentially return against Crystal Palace next Sunday, it suggests that the midfielder’s injury is relatively minor.

The 24-year-old mightn’t make it back in time for the visit to Selhurst Park, but the two-week international window should hopefully enable him to be fully fit for the grudge match against Manchester United later this month.

The Dutchman was criticised for his performance against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup last week and in recent games has been disapponting by his standards, but he remains a vital player to Liverpool and one of the best midfielders in the Premier League when operating at his top level.

Even if he’s cleared to play on Sunday, Gravenberch seems unlikely to start given the form of Alexis Mac Allister and Trey Nyoni in the middle of the park, and he mightn’t be able to feature for a full 90 minutes if he’s touch-and-go for the weekend.

Fingers crossed that our number 38 will at least be available to Iraola when the Reds take on Palace with one eye on revenge for their last-gasp defeat in this fixture last season.
